Because the paragraph has no bullet numbers, every step cites source_bullets [1] meaning 'the single walkthrough paragraph'; that is the convention for this record and it is stated here so the audit stays honest.

The wait for the bomb is not given its own rung: it is a pause, not an action, and it is unmarkable and unobservable.

The two Notes bullets are not steps -- one says the ??? works even with no fortification present and no battle running, the other is a failure mode (the ??? resetting mid-bomb, after which it says 'You find nothing out of the ordinary'). gates.level is 70 from the header's 'Level: 70+'. Campaign Rank is {{question}} in the wikitext, i.e. the wiki does not know it, so no rank is asserted. repeatable is null: campaign ops generally are, but this page never says so. No expansion field exists on the Campaign Header template, so expansion is null rather than assumed.

notes:
This page genuinely has no walkthrough -- the cached wikitext is the {{Campaign Header}} call and nothing else, no ==Walkthrough==, no Notes, no sections at all. Unlike the two Windurst pages above, there is no dropped prose to recover.

What the page does have is a populated Orders field, and it is real player instruction rather than flavour: a lead line 'Join a Campaign Battle in a Windurst-controlled area.' and two sub-bullets, 'Earn a total of 2000 Allied Notes with Allied Tags.' and 'When enough points have been earned, the message "Objective completed. Report to Emhi Tchaoryo in Windurst Waters." will appear when Allied Tags wear off.' The two steps below are read from those. source_bullets [1] and [2] refer to the two Orders sub-bullets in order; the lead line is unnumbered and is folded into [1], where it belongs. That convention is stated here because there is no walkthrough numbering to cite.

No sign-up step is invented. The header's NPC Name is Emhi Tchaoryo and the completion message names him as the person to report to, so start carries him, but nothing on the page instructs the player to talk to him first and a rung on that would be authored rather than read. The battle step gets no zone: 'a Windurst-controlled area' is a set that rotates with the front line, and the 2000-Allied-Note threshold is a running total, not a location.

Campaign Rank 'Mythril Wings of Service' is a campaign rank, not a character level -- it is deliberately kept out of gates.level, which means character level, and flagged instead. Header Level is 'Any' so gates.level is null. repeatable null: the page does not say.

steps.note: join a Campaign Battle in a Windurst-controlled area and earn a total of 2000 Allied Notes with Allied Tags up; the eligible zones rotate with front-line control so none is recorded. [1] = the first Orders sub-bullet plus its unnumbered lead line.
report only once 'Objective completed. Report to Emhi Tchaoryo in Windurst Waters.' appears, which happens when the Allied Tags wear off. [2] = the second Orders sub-bullet.

notes:
Not a fight at all -- this is a crafting quiz, and reading it as a combat op because its siblings are would be exactly the pattern-match this pipeline exists to avoid. You are handed off to an Adjutant, you pick a craft, and he asks you the recipe for three synths in that craft, one question at a time.

Bullets [2] and [3] are one rung, not two: both happen in one conversation with the Adjutant (pick a craft, then answer the three tests), and [3]'s six sub-bullets are the wordings of the questions he asks -- 'What crystal is used for this synth?', 'What is the first ingredient...' -- which are dialogue, not player actions.

ZONE JUDGEMENT ON STEP 2: the page gives the Adjutant's grid, (F-9), twice -- in bullet [1] and in the header Description -- but never his zone. Windurst Waters (S) is taken from the header, where this op's own NPC stands at (H-9); the walkthrough forwards you to the Adjutant straight out of that conversation. Flagged, and the step is medium, because it is an inference rather than a statement.

Repeatable is TRUE here and is the one record in this batch where the page says so outright: Notes [1], 'This is repeatable (as long as you have tags)'. Campaign Rank 'Brass Wings of Service' is restated in Notes [3] as an access requirement; it is a campaign rank, not a character level, so it stays out of gates.level and is flagged. Header Level is 'Any'.

Notes [2] is a warning about a sub-45-second answer timer starting the line after the Adjutant names the recipe -- advice, and it is also what Time: Yes in the header refers to. It is not a time-of-day gate. The page also carries a ==Recipes== table which is almost entirely an unfilled stub ('Item name' / 'Ingredients' placeholders) with only three real Goldsmithing rows, so the quiz answers are effectively undocumented; that is a wiki gap, not a step.

steps.note: he forwards you to the Adjutant at (F-9)

A fixed-location op, so unlike the campaign-battle ops in this batch every rung below carries a real position. Entry is a named object at a stated grid: the Beastman Ensign at (G-12) in Grauberg. The page spells it 'Beastman' (singular, and as a wikilink); Pit Spider III (B) and By Light of Fire I (B), which use the same entry point, spell it 'Beastmen Ensign'. Each record keeps its own page's spelling -- the resolver folds names to keys and does not check that either exists, so silently harmonising them would be editing the source rather than reading it.

MOB COUNTS ARE ARITHMETIC THE PAGE SUPPORTS, NOT A GUESS. Bullet [3] gives the per-party composition, '2x Quadav Guard, 1x Quadav Carrier', says there are two such parties, and states the total independently: 'kill all 6 Quadavs'. 2x(2+1) = 6 matches, so 4 Guards and 2 Carriers is defensible in both directions. (Pit Spider III (B) states a different composition and a different total, 4x Guard + 1x Carrier per party and ten in all; the two pages are not interchangeable and neither was copied onto the other.)

Bullet [3]'s two sub-bullets are mob behaviour and a FAIL condition -- Carriers flee when engaged or at low HP, and the op fails if one reaches the end of its route -- not steps. Bullet [4]'s sub-bullet, by contrast, IS a step and is kept: 'You must exit area by using the Twilight Aureola for Hieronymus to acknowledge the mission as successful!' -- leaving through it is a required action, not commentary.

GRID CONFLICT ACROSS PAGES: this page puts Hieronymus at (I-9), as do Pit Spider III (B) and By Light of Fire I (B); the six other Bastok campaign-op pages in this batch put him at (E-8). Recorded as this page states it, and flagged so a human can settle it against the game.

notes:
Same two-rung shape as Aegis Scream III (B) and IV (B), but bullet [1] is materially different and that difference is the whole point of reading rather than pattern-matching: this one is not a defence of a Bastokan stronghold, it is a Campaign battle 'in any Northlands allied controlled region' -- an offensive op in the north, matching the Description ('a series of attacks on northern Confederate strongholds'). The Campaign Type field still says 'Defensive operations', which contradicts both the bullet and the Description; the bullet is the instruction, so the bullet is what the step records, and the contradiction is why this is medium rather than high.

ZONE: still none, and doubly so here -- the region must be ALLIED-held (the reverse of the beastman-held condition on most ops in this batch) and Notes [1] says the op only appears at all when Beaucedine Glacier (S) or Xarcabard (S) is under allied control. Those two are availability conditions naming candidate zones, not a stated location for the step, and control rotates, so they are noted rather than recorded. No mobs; the page names none.

[2] and [3] are one rung: report to Hieronymus, and only after the 'Objective Completed' message, because [3] says reporting early fails the op. NO SIGN-UP BULLET: the walkthrough never sends you to Hieronymus first; start carries him from the header and no rung is invented.
